headline: GOLD REBOUNDS TO $4,400 AS DOLLAR EASES — SILVER LEADS AHEAD OF FRIDAY'S INFLATION PRINT
snippet: Gold clawed back to $4,399.61 (+1.02%) and silver outperformed at $66.58 (+1.23%) on Wednesday as the U.S. dollar softened following a punishing three-session slide that had sent 10-year Treasury yields to roughly 4.77%, their highest since 2008. Analysts note the recovery was a mechanical currency repricing — not a safe-haven bid — meaning gold remains pinned below its 55- and 200-day moving averages, with Friday's CPI print the next key catalyst for direction.

headline: MARIMACA COPPER DRILLS 216M AT 2.2% CU AT PAMPA MEDINA — STOCK SURGES 13% AS STEP-OUTS EXTEND SYSTEM
snippet: Marimaca Copper (TSX: MARI, ASX: MC2) released new assays from its Pampa Medina deposit in Chile's Antofagasta Region: SPRD-15 returned 216m at 1.0% Cu and 7.2 g/t Ag from 466m depth, including 62m at 2.20% Cu and 21.5 g/t Ag — among the thickest and highest-grade copper-silver intervals drilled to date. Step-out holes SPRD-12, SPD-13, and SPRD-17 extended the mineralized sulphide horizon 300m to the south and west of the defined 3km × 1.5km central corridor, sending Marimaca shares to a TSX top-gainer position with a 13% intraday surge.

headline: HOT CHILI CONFIRMS THICK HIGH-GRADE ENRICHMENT AT LA VERDE — 62M AT 0.91% CUEQ FROM JUST 20M DEPTH
snippet: Hot Chili (ASX: HCH, TSXV: HCH) reported three high-grade shallow intersections from new reverse circulation drilling at the La Verde copper-gold porphyry discovery in Chile's coastal Atacama region. Headline hole DKP063 returned 62m at 0.91% CuEq (0.70% Cu, 0.30 g/t Au) from 20m depth within a 398m envelope at 0.45% CuEq from surface — confirming wide near-surface enrichment extending across the deposit. La Verde sits 30km south of Hot Chili's Costa Fuego processing hub; assays from 22 additional holes remain pending.

headline: GOLDGROUP MINING HITS 10.9M AT 6.34 G/T AU AT SAN FRANCISCO — RESTART STUDY LAUNCHES ON 26,000M PROGRAM
snippet: Goldgroup Mining (TSXV: GORO, NYSE Arca: GORO) released first assays from its 26,000m diamond drilling program at the formerly producing San Francisco Gold Project in Sonora, Mexico: GGD-174 returned 23.4m at 1.71 g/t Au, GGD-178 cut 16.8m at 4.36 g/t Au and 10.0m at 2.00 g/t Au, and GGD-181 intersected 10.9m at 6.34 g/t Au. Results are being fed into updated geological and resource models to support a detailed restart and optimization study backed by an approximately US$8.5 million budget.

headline: STANMORE BAGS 724MT OF PREMIUM COKING COAL IN $145M MORANBAH SOUTH DEAL — BOWEN BASIN EMPIRE EXPANDS
snippet: Stanmore Resources agreed to acquire 100% of the Moranbah South (MBS) tenements in Queensland's Bowen Basin from Exxaro Resources for US$105 million (A$145 million), adding 724 million tonnes of measured and indicated Goonyella Middle Seam coking coal immediately adjacent to its Eagle Downs and Isaac Downs Extension projects. The deal came together via a complex chain: Exxaro exercised joint venture pre-emption rights over Anglo American's 50% MBS stake, then flipped the whole asset to Stanmore. Completion is expected before year-end, subject to FIRB, ACCC, and ministerial approvals.

headline: CHILE PASSES SENATE BILL OPENING CAPITAL MARKETS TO JUNIOR EXPLORERS — WORLD'S TOP COPPER NATION COURTS EARLY-STAGE CAPITAL
snippet: Chile's Senate approved legislation creating a dedicated investment framework for junior exploration and innovation companies, including tax incentives and relaxed listing requirements. The Kast administration says the bill directly addresses the financing bottleneck keeping juniors out of Chile — the world's largest copper producer and second-largest lithium supplier — where exploration spending reached US$874 million in 2025 but remained concentrated in majors. Analysts see the move as a structural positive for TSX-V and ASX juniors with Chilean assets.

headline: AZTEC MINERALS EXTENDS TOMBSTONE OXIDE GOLD STRIKE TO 1,250M — 83.8M AT 1.31 G/T AUEQ, RESOURCE DUE Q4
snippet: Aztec Minerals (CVE: AZT) extended the Contention mineralized system at its Tombstone Property in southeastern Arizona to over 1,250m of continuously drilled strike length. Five new RC holes all intersected oxide gold-silver mineralization, led by TR26-41 returning 83.8m at 1.31 g/t AuEq (0.90 g/t Au, 22.61 g/t Ag) including 7.6m at 8.34 g/t AuEq; the extension adds 255m from the previous southernmost hole with no barren intercept. A maiden resource estimate is scheduled for Q4 2026 as drilling moves to test nine additional holes for which assays remain pending.

headline: GDX DROPS 12.4% WHILE GOLD SLIPS 6.7% — HISTORY SAYS THE LEVERAGE DIVERGENCE IS A BUY SIGNAL
snippet: Seeking Alpha analysis notes that the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) has now declined roughly twice as much as physical gold during the recent pullback — 12.4% versus gold's 6.7% — compressing valuations to an 11.2x P/E with robust expected EPS growth. The author argues this miner-versus-metal divergence, which historically precedes mean-reversion outperformance by producers, creates a compelling entry point for investors willing to hold through the September 16 Federal Reserve meeting, with the key risk being a decisive hike pushing gold below the $4,380 support zone.

headline: GOLD STOCKS' AUTUMN RALLY '26: SEASONAL SETUP BUILDS FOR OCTOBER BREAKOUT AS GDX CLEARS KEY RESISTANCE
snippet: GoldSeek analysis reviews the seasonal pattern for gold equities heading into autumn 2026, noting that the NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index posted its best August since 1994 (+33%) before giving back gains in September, and that the GDX has already cleared several prior-year resistance highs that gold itself has not yet matched. The piece argues that the combination of still-positive seasonal tailwinds, extreme miner undervaluation relative to the metal, and approaching catalysts — September 16 FOMC, October conference season — makes the September dip the highest-probability setup for the next equity leg of the gold bull market.

headline: CAMECO + KAZATOMPROM CUTS STOKE URANIUM MARKET TIGHTNESS — STRUCTURAL DEFICIT DEEPENS AMID NUCLEAR BUILDOUT
snippet: Fresh analysis from Nasdaq highlights how simultaneous production guidance cuts from the world's two largest uranium suppliers — Kazatomprom's roughly 10% reduction in 2026 output (to 27,500–29,000 tU) citing sulphuric acid constraints, and Cameco's McArthur River ramp slower than expected — are deepening a structural supply deficit just as reactor demand accelerates. With spot uranium near $89.65/lb and price targets rising to $95, capital is flowing back into uranium equities; Sprott's junior uranium index returned 21.75% in a single month as investors front-run what analysts call the next contracting cycle.
